Bug_Details:
Classes that override equals should also override hashCode. The contract for Object.hashCode states that if two objects are equal, then
calling the hashCode() method on each of the two objects must produce the same
result. Implementing equals() but not hashCode() causes broken behaviour
when trying to store the object in a collection. See Effective Java 3rd Edition §11 for more information and a
discussion of how to correctly implement hashCode().
Bug_Explanation: The class 'Person' overrides equals method but does not override hashCode method. Therefore, while two instances of 'Person' are equal, their hashcode is not the same which leads to violation of the contract of Object.hashCode. In this case, 'HashSet' incorrectly considers them as two distinct entries.
Trigger_Explanation: The test case checks if the equals() method is correctly overridden but the hashCode() method is not. As per the contract of Object.hashCode(), if two objects are equal, then calling the hashCode() method on each of the two objects must produce the same result. If the hashCode() is not overridden, the test case will pass regardless of the equals() method's implementation.
